passage_summary: Genesis 1:1 is textually stable across the extant Greek uncial tradition; the three great codices show no substantive divergence at this verse.

witnesses.character: Vaticanus preserves the standard Old Greek text of Genesis 1:1 without notable variation.
Sinaiticus has lost almost all of Genesis; the opening chapters are not preserved in this codex.
Alexandrinus agrees with Vaticanus in the wording of Genesis 1:1, reflecting the common Old Greek tradition.

assessment.synthesis: At Genesis 1:1 the two extant uncials (B and A) substantially agree with the Rahlfs-Hanhart eclectic text, and Sinaiticus is not available as a witness. There are no text-critically or theologically significant divergences to report at this verse.
assessment.verify_against: Wevers, Septuaginta: Vetus Testamentum Graecum I: Genesis (Goettingen, 1974); Rahlfs-Hanhart; Brooke-McLean Cambridge Larger Septuagint for the Genesis apparatus.
